name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: Tankers hit by mines off Khasab 26 Nov
summary: Iran's Guards say two tankers hit mines off Oman's Khasab on 26 Nov; UKMTO reports a blast near a tanker west of Dubai
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on 26 Nov that two tankers, one a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels of crude, exploded and caught fire after hitting mines north of Oman's Khasab while using an unauthorised route through Hormuz, and that the strait stays closed (Arab News). UKMTO reported an explosion from an unknown projectile near a tanker about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai the same day (Times of Israel). Attacks on shipping keep the Alert.
for_you: Shipping, fuel and insurance costs stay exposed to Gulf disruption. Travellers to the region should follow FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Attacks on Gulf shipping (mine strikes 26 Nov) = Alert

sources.title: Arab News — Two oil tankers hit mines north of Oman's Khasab port, IRGC says
Times of Israel — Projectile said to cause explosion near tanker west of Dubai

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
